# Ruby Gillis

## Overview

- **Age:** 18 at death  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v3 c14 P0](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0000), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased (died of galloping consumption)  <sub>[v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher  <sub>[v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Ruby was exceptionally handsome, with a brilliant complexion, large blue eyes, and long, thick, golden hair. She possessed a plump, showy figure, and was considered one of the handsomest girls of her year. During her illness she grew very thin and pale with hectically brilliant cheeks, though she retained her striking beauty until her death.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c25 P0](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0000), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P31](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0031)_

## Personality

Ruby was cheerful, good-tempered, and loved the pleasant things of life, though she was undeniably shallow, vain, and sentimental. She had an hysterical streak and was prone to fits of tears or laughter. Obsessed with boys, courtships, and beaux from a young age, she measured her success by her romantic conquests. She fought hard against accepting her fatal illness, maintaining a cheerful facade until she finally faced her fear of death in a tender confession to Anne.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v1 c26 P5](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0005), [v1 c26 P6](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0006), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)_

## History

Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea as a schoolmate of Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. During their schooldays, she was known for her beauty, her numerous beaux, and her tendency to turn hysterical in emergencies. She joined the girls' Story Club, contributing overly sentimental tales. After studying for the Entrance at Avonlea School, she attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne and earned a teacher's license. She taught for a time in Carmody, where she continued her active romantic pursuits, but contracted a severe lung congestion during the winter. This developed into galloping consumption, forcing her to quit teaching. Throughout her illness, Ruby maintained a cheerful front and insisted she would recover to teach at White Sands. Shortly before her death, she broke down to Anne Shirley, confessing her terror of dying and her grief at leaving the world behind. She passed away calmly in her sleep that autumn and was buried in the Avonlea graveyard.

## Quotes

> I’m not afraid but that I’ll go to heaven, Anne. I’m a church member. But—it’ll be all so different. I think—and think—and I get so frightened—and—and—homesick.  <sub>[v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)</sub>

> I want to live. I want to live like other girls. I—I want to be married, Anne—and—and—have little children.  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>

> When I was in bed—if I could’ve slept I’d have dreamed of you, Anne.  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)</sub>

> I was that scared I actshally couldn’t speak.  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)</sub>
